## Features

- **Pitch-locked scratching**: small slices of the audio (grains) always play at normal speed, so the pitch stays the same even when you play backwards or freeze.
- **Video follows the audio**: the edit cursor follows the scratch position, and the video window shows that frame.
- **Built-in all-intra (every frame a keyframe) conversion**: H.264 video, which is slow to seek and play backwards, can be converted to fast-seeking MJPEG with REAPER alone (if FFmpeg is on the PC, it is used automatically so that no frames shift).
- **Works with many MIDI controllers**: the Reloop Buddy and the APC40 mkII (tested on the real hardware), other DJ controllers such as the DDJ-FLX4 (presets not yet tested on the hardware are marked ⚠︎ in the preset list), encoders, and even ordinary MIDI knobs.
- **Crossfader cuts**: open and close the sound instantly with the crossfader (chirps, transformers and so on). You can set where the sound starts (the cut-in gap) and how much fader travel is required to open fully. While the sound is cut, the video disappears too.
- **8 hot cues**: store positions on the pads (keys `1`–`8`) and jump to them. A short press jumps and keeps playing; a long press returns to where you were when you let go (press PLAY while holding to keep playing after release). Positions are saved in the project.
- **Memory cues (up to 32)**: like rekordbox / CDJ memory cues, store many positions and step back and forth through them with `CALL`. The recalled position becomes the CUE point (while playing, it jumps and keeps playing; while stopped, it moves there and stays stopped). Positions are saved in the project.
- **SLIP mode**: when on, playback keeps running in the background while you scratch or hold a hot cue. When you let go, playback continues from "where it would have been if you had not touched anything" (like SLIP on rekordbox / CDJs). Off by default.
- **Beat-quantized jumps (quantize)**: when on, hot cues, memory cue CALL, the return when you release a held hot cue, and CUE all jump on the next beat instead of the moment you press, while playing (same as QUANTIZE on rekordbox / CDJs). Presses up to 0.03 s after a beat jump at once. BPM and beat positions are estimated automatically when a video is imported. If the estimate fails, tap the `T` key or the `bpm` box on the screen on the beat while playing, or type the BPM into the `bpm` box (while stopped, or with Shift+click). You can also set them in setup. Off by default.
- **Sample switching (up to 8)**: import up to 8 videos and switch between them instantly with the `1`–`8` buttons at the bottom of the screen, the `F1`–`F8` keys, or the DDJ-FLX4 pads (`SAMPLER` mode). Each sample remembers its last play position, CUE, hot cues, memory cues and BPM, and resumes where it left off when you come back. The play/stop state is kept too. With SLIP on, samples you are not using keep running in the background while playing, and when you come back they play from "where they would be if they had kept playing".
- **Two decks plus crossfader to layer video (deck B)**: create a second deck (deck B) during setup and the crossfader moves smoothly between the two decks' sound and video. Video is composited with REAPER's built-in Video processor. You can choose the blend around the middle (Mix, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Overlay, Soft light, Hard light, Luma key or Chroma key) and a transition, where the crossfader's movement replaces one picture with the other (29 types such as wipes, zooms and spins). On the DDJ-FLX4, deck B is played from the right deck (Deck 2).
- **Tempo and SYNC**: change the playback speed without changing the pitch (range ±8%, ±16% or ±50%, or ±5 to ±60 BPM; default ±20 BPM). The video stretches with it. The `sync` button (`BEAT SYNC` on the DDJ-FLX4) matches the other deck's BPM and lines up the beats (same as BEAT SYNC in rekordbox; when the BPMs are close to double or half, it matches at double or half). For example, set two samples to the same BPM and switch between them on the beat.
- **Songs whose tempo changes**: for live recordings and other songs whose tempo wavers or changes partway, the beat positions can be kept as a map (the same idea as rekordbox's dynamic beat grid). A map is made in three ways: when importing a video or with LOAD, the beats are followed one by one and the tempo turns out to move (songs with a steady tempo keep one BPM as before); when rekordbox's XML has tempo changes; and when you press `Shift`+`T` where the grid is off while playing. Everything that uses beats (beat-synced jumps, loops, SYNC, the beat lines, the LFOs, and so on) follows the map. The BPM readout shows the BPM where the playback is, and SYNC keeps matching the other deck's tempo where it is playing. Typing the BPM again or tapping it with `T` goes back to one tempo
- **Musical key and KEY SYNC**: when a video is imported or loaded with LOAD, its key is detected and shown in the `key` window above the word `grain`, like `Am` (white for the sample's own key; with the key knob turned, the key you hear, in the lamp colour, and the semitones in small text at the window's top right). A `?` after it means the detection was a close call. Click the window or press `U` to turn the key knob so this deck matches the other deck's key (KEY SYNC: the same key or its relative, such as Am and C, the nearer way, up to 6 semitones). `Shift`+click or `Shift`+`U` goes back to the sample's own key. The detection is libKeyFinder's method (the one Mixxx uses) ported to Lua: on 120 EDM test tracks it found the same key for 57%, and most of the others were close keys (a fifth away or the relative). Check by ear before relying on it.
- **Metronome**: a click on the beats of a deck (the first beat of each bar higher). REAPER's own metronome only sounds while REAPER plays, and the decks play with REAPER stopped, so ReaScratch makes its own. It sounds in the headphones only (or in the main output too), and follows the playing deck, the SYNC base deck, or each deck. Turn it on/off with the `N` key, a click on the window in the record's corner, or a MIDI button (see [“Listening to a metronome while you play”](listening-to-a-metronome-while-you-play.md)).
- **Video effects (15 types)**: colour (Tint, Hue rotate, Invert, Threshold), shape (Mirror, Kaleidoscope, LoRez, Shift RGB, Disc, Zoom blur), redrawn pictures (Line art, Halftone), beat-synced (Strobe, Trails) and an old videotape look (VHS), on each deck's picture and on the mixed picture (in projects that have deck B). Their amounts can also rise and fall with the beat (LFO). Each video effect also comes with a matching sound effect (echo, bitcrusher, chorus and so on).
- **Pad modes, loops and filter**: besides hot cues, the pads can play auto loops, effects while held (TOUCH FX), a slicer, short loops (BOUNCE LOOP) and pitch (PITCH PLAY). There is also CUE LOOP, which starts a loop from a hot cue's position, and a DJ filter (8 types; turning it also changes the colour tone of the layered picture) (on the Reloop Buddy, the APC40 mkII and many other presets).
- **Brake and spinback**: a brake that slows down gradually when you stop with PLAY (its length in seconds or in beats), PAUSE quantize that makes the stop wait for the beat, a motor start-up when playback starts (all off by default), and a spinback on the `B` key that throws the record backwards and slows to a stop.
- **Scratching from envelopes (patterns)**: write the record movement and the crossfader into REAPER envelopes and the deck scratches exactly that when it plays the section. Place the included patterns (baby, chirp, tear, flare, transformer and more) as automation items, rearrange them by copying, moving and editing points, and save them as your own patterns. Play while recording in REAPER and your jog and crossfader movements are written to the envelopes, so you can replay them later.
- **Try it without a controller**: in the JSFX window, grab the record with the mouse and turn it, or drag the zoomed waveform, to scratch; click or drag the whole-track waveform to search; use the PC keyboard for play/stop, CUE and freeze.
- **Loading cues from rekordbox**: load the hot cues, memory cues, BPM and beat grid, and key from an XML exported from rekordbox. Traktor's and VirtualDJ's track data can be loaded too ([“Loading cues from rekordbox”](basic-use.md#loading-cues-from-rekordbox), “Traktor and VirtualDJ track data”). You can also write a sample's cues and BPM out to an XML for rekordbox or to ReaScratch track data (“Writing out track data”).
- **Loading with the LOAD button**: put a video or audio file chosen in the Media Explorer into a deck while you play (Windows). An audio-only file shows a spinning speaker picture instead of video ([“Loading with the LOAD button (from the Media Explorer)”](basic-use.md#loading-with-the-load-button-from-the-media-explorer)). You can also drag a file from the Media Explorer or the Windows Explorer onto a deck's JSFX window ([“Loading by dragging a file”](basic-use.md#loading-by-dragging-a-file)).
- **Previewing a Media Explorer file**: the `P` key (on many controllers, a button too) previews the file chosen in the Media Explorer. The sound goes to the headphones only and the picture to the centre of the deck's record only, never to the video window ([“Previewing a Media Explorer file (P key)”](basic-use.md#previewing-a-media-explorer-file-p-key)).
- **Headphones, capture and your own presets**: you can also listen ahead on headphones to a deck the crossfader has cut ([“Listening to a deck on headphones (Cue)”](listening-to-a-deck-on-headphones-cue.md)), turn a performance into each deck's sound and video plus the finished video ([“Capturing a performance”](scratching-from-envelopes-patterns.md#capturing-a-performance)), and make the settings for a controller without a preset on setup's `Learn` tab ([“Check by touch / make a preset”](controller-setup-and-midi-mapping.md#check-by-touch--make-a-preset-setup-learn-tab)).

### How it differs from other DJ software

ReaScratch has the same controls as rekordbox and other DJ software, such as hot cues, SLIP, quantize and SYNC. On top of that, it has the following points for making otoMAD videos, which other DJ software mostly does not have.

- **Scratching without a pitch change**: grains always play at normal speed, so the pitch stays the same when you scratch or stop. The `pitch ─ tape` bar under the record changes it smoothly all the way to a record-like pitch that follows the speed ([“Reading the screen”](jsfx-reascratch-parameter-reference.md#reading-the-screen)).
- **A performance captured as material to edit**: each deck's sound, and video cut and joined to match the exact frames the deck showed, are laid out as a REAPER project. With ffmpeg, it also makes mp4 files with no shifted frames ([“Capturing a performance”](scratching-from-envelopes-patterns.md#capturing-a-performance)).
- **Scratches you program**: place techniques such as the baby and the chirp as patterns on the beat, fit them to the track's swing, rearrange and save them, and play them from the pads ([“Scratching from envelopes (patterns)”](scratching-from-envelopes-patterns.md), [“Fitting the swing”](scratching-from-envelopes-patterns.md#fitting-the-swing)).
- **Fix a performance afterwards**: your hand movements and the crossfader are recorded into envelopes (automation items), and you can fix the details by moving points ([“Recording a performance into envelopes”](scratching-from-envelopes-patterns.md#recording-a-performance-into-envelopes)).
- **Decks inside a DAW**: a deck is a REAPER track, so you can add other effects (VST and so on) to that track. Decks can play side by side with song tracks, in time with REAPER's tempo (`REAPER tempo` in [“9. Beat-quantized jumps”](jsfx-reascratch-parameter-reference.md#9-beat-quantized-jumps-setup-beat-tab)). A recorded performance is saved as a project and can be rendered in REAPER.
- **Video effects for otoMAD**: each of the 15 video effects comes with a matching sound effect. The crossfader controls 9 blends and 29 transitions between the two decks ([“Sound and video effects”](pad-modes-loops-filter-and-effects.md#sound-and-video-effects), [“Two decks with layered video”](two-decks-with-layered-video-deck-b.md)).
- **Many controllers**: there are 122 presets. Even old models and the APC40, which is not a DJ controller, can play two decks from one unit. For a controller without a preset, you can make your own on setup's `Learn` tab ([“Preset list”](controller-setup-and-midi-mapping.md#preset-list), [“Check by touch / make a preset”](controller-setup-and-midi-mapping.md#check-by-touch--make-a-preset-setup-learn-tab)).
- **Working with other DJ software and hardware**: hot cues, memory cues, BPM and beat grid, and key can be loaded from a collection XML exported from rekordbox ([“Loading cues from rekordbox”](basic-use.md#loading-cues-from-rekordbox)). NI Traktor Kontrol controllers that talk HID (S4 MK3, S3, S2 MK3 and others) connect through the included bridge program ([“HID controllers”](controller-setup-and-midi-mapping.md#hid-controllers-ni-traktor-kontrol-s4-s3-s2)). There are also presets for the CDJ-2000NXS2 and CDJ-3000 as MIDI controllers (not yet tested on the hardware).
- **Free**: ReaScratch is free, and under GPL-3.0-or-later you may change it and share it ([“License & credits”](license-credits.md)). REAPER keeps working after its 60-day evaluation, but if you keep using it, you are expected to buy a license (60 US dollars for personal use).
